the metallic electrodes are very effective in reducing the e-cloud effects on the beam dynamics and the vacuum chamber resonant frequencies.
the metallic electrodes are able to mitigate the e-cloud impact, and that the e-cloud is not completely suppressed.
the e-cloud mitigation is effective in DAne, that the electrodes reduce the e-cloud density and that the electrodes are able to mitigate the e-cloud induced beam instability and tune shift.

the experimental investigation of e-cloud induced effects in the DANE collider.
the development of a new technique to control the e-cloud in high intensity accelerators.
the experimental measurements of the electron-cloud effects and the effectiveness of the clearing electrodes in suppressing them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the e-cloud mitigation strategy adopted in the DANE collider is effective and the electrodes are a valid and efficient solution for the e-cloud problem.
the electrodes are effective in mitigating the electron cloud effects and in improving the beam stability and luminosity.
the clearing electrodes have a strong positive effect on the positron dynamics in DA NE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DANE collider is the first electron-positron storage ring where e-cloud mitigation techniques have been successfully applied and tested.
the electrodes allow to reduce the e-cloud density by a factor 2.5-4.
the electrodes allow us to run with an electron cloud density 1 order of magnitude lower than the one observed during the previous run without electrodes.

the electrodes have a strong impact on the beam dynamics and the vacuum chamber resonant frequencies.
the clearing electrodes are an effective and simple way to mitigate the e-cloud effects in high intensity electron-positron colliders.
